newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK CARDICO SEES STRONG EXPORTS IN 97.
newsitem.headline: GREEK CARDICO SEES STRONG EXPORTS IN 97.

text.p: Greek Cardico, an importer and processor of dried nuts and fruits, saw strong export growth in eastern European countries last year and expects earnings growth of 50 percent in 1997, its management told reporters.
"Our fiscal 1996 results exceeded earlier projections as sales rose to 6.2 billion drachmas against an earlier forecast of 5.6 billion," said managing director Nick Kardasilaris.
A recent listing on the Athens bourse's small-cap parallel market, Cardico said pretax profit rose 4.0 percent to 500 million drachmas.

Last year it exported 25 percent of its output to eastern European countries including Poland, Romania, the Czech Republic and Moldavia. France and Italy in western Europe also absorbed a large part of 1996 sales.
The company which is supplied by co-operatives and imports processes and packages a wide variety of nuts including almonds, walnuts, hazelnuts, peanuts and pistachios.
It intends to pay a fiscal 1996 dividend per share of 150 drachmas.

Its main industrial processing is nut shelling and blanching. The distribution of product in Greece is carried out through wholesalers who in turn supply distributors of pastry raw materials and nuts.
Clients include the confectionery and chocolate industries, and makers of ice-cream.
Cardico management expects sales growth of 29 percent this year, around 8.0 billion drachmas and pretax profit of 750 million, up 50 percent.
"In the first two months of the year we are experiencing sales growth of 100 percent," Kardasilaris said.
It recently completed investment in Moldavia to process walnut kernels will have an output capacity of 2,000 tonnes. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
